v.story-r.intro.1.text: Bossy-R Mountains are tall and rocky, and the r there is very bossy.

v.story-r.intro.2.text: An r right after a vowel takes charge and changes the sound that vowel makes.

v.story-r.intro.3.text: Climb the mountain path, find the torn pages, and listen to what the bossy r tells the vowel to do.

v.story-r.r-ar-or.1.text: A garden grows on the mountainside, and ar in its name makes a sound all its own.

v.story-r.r-ar-or.2.text: Or works the same way, so a fork at the picnic table teaches the bossy r sound.

v.story-r.r-er-ir-ur.1.text: A bird sits on a perch, and its name has er, ir and ur, which sound alike.

v.story-r.r-er-ir-ur.2.text: Er, ir and ur all make the same sound, so the bird's song hides three spellings for one note.

v.story-r.r-mix.1.text: A carpenter builds a shelter on the mountain, and the tool list has ar, or, er, ir and ur.

v.story-r.r-mix.2.text: Read each bossy r word one part at a time, and the mountain shelter stands tall.

v.story-r.finale.1.text: The mountains are quiet, and the bossy r pages shine in the Great Word Book.

v.story-r.finale.2.text: The Keeper says, 'Little Tail Lake is next, where a little l and a silent e hide at the ends of words.'
